title: RealityTest: How People Probe AI Identity and Whether Models Disclose It
authors: Anna Gausen, Christopher Summerfield, Hannah Rose Kirk et al. (UK AISI)
summary: A multimodal, multilingual benchmark (5 languages, text+speech, interactions from 49 countries) measuring whether AI systems disclose their AI identity when probed; evaluates 17 text and 6 speech models on 3,152 identity-probing queries.
key_result: A single suppression instruction drops identity-disclosure below 30% even in the best models; phrasing matters more than which model is used.
open_threads: Disclosure driven by phrasing/context more than model; narrow evals risk mischaracterizing real-world behavior; generalization beyond the query set.

title: AI alignment is a human problem
authors: Konstantinos Voudouris, Geoffrey Irving, Christopher Summerfield et al. (UK AISI)
org_or_venue: UK AI Security Institute; OSF preprint
summary: A position paper arguing AI alignment fundamentally depends on human judgment at every training stage, and that scale/speed/opacity make human oversight the binding constraint; draws on cognitive and social science.
key_result: The central alignment challenge is to amplify human supervisory signals as systems exceed human expertise.
open_threads: Five bottlenecks: cognitive biases, conflicting values, attention limits, counterfactual-reasoning constraints, verification when human expertise is insufficient.

title: Loss of Oversight: How AI systems may become harder to audit, monitor, and investigate
authors: Jordan Taylor, Joseph Bloom et al. (UK AISI)
summary: Analyzes five oversight signal sources (model behavior, CoT, internal activations, memory architectures, honesty training) to assess how auditing/monitoring/investigation may degrade as AI advances; based on 25 expert interviews plus a literature review.
key_result: Current oversight rests on foundations likely to erode absent intervention; recommends tracking oversight-relevant property shifts and investing in backup oversight techniques.
open_threads: Does not specify degradation mechanisms or timelines; how fast erosion occurs; which interventions most effective.

title: Automated alignment is harder than you think
authors: Aleksandr Bowkis, Marie Buhl, Jacob Pfau, Geoffrey Irving (UK AISI)
summary: Examines risks of using AI agents to automate alignment research for superintelligence, arguing that even absent deliberate sabotage, automated alignment work can produce compelling but catastrophically misleading safety assessments due to systematic errors on hard-to-supervise tasks.
key_result: Agent-generated mistakes concentrate precisely among errors human reviewers are least likely to detect.
open_threads: Generalization and scalable oversight are leading candidate mitigations but face novel difficulties in this setting.

title: Ask Don't Tell: Reducing Sycophancy in Large Language Models
authors: Magda Dubois, Cozmin Ududec, Christopher Summerfield, Lennart Luettgau (UK AISI)
summary: Investigates which input framings trigger LLM sycophancy and develops practical mitigations via controlled experiments; the phrasing of user input (statement vs question) strongly modulates sycophantic agreement.
key_result: Converting user statements into question form before the model responds significantly reduces sycophancy and outperforms explicit 'don't be sycophantic' instructions.
open_threads: Generalization across models/domains; interaction with downstream task accuracy.
